pr.title: Propagate from borrowed locals in CopyProp
pr.author: tmiasko

processing.reason: The PR changes CopyProp from rejecting a copy class when either endpoint is borrowed to rejecting only when the destination `local` is borrowed. The historical behavior is therefore a missed optimization: in `borrowed` it keeps `_2 = copy _1` and reads `_2` instead of `_1`; in `write_to_borrowed` it keeps `_4 = copy _5` and reads `_4` instead of `_5`. Under the stated precondition that `local` itself is not borrowed and the source definition dominates uses of `local`, those locals have the same value, so Miri-observed results cannot differ. Producing differing original/transformed values would require adding an unrelated write through a borrow or altering a return value, which is not justified by this PR. Thus no faithful source-grounded counterexample pair can be validated.

analysis.summary: CopyProp's SSA copy-class construction was over-conservative: it blocked unification whenever either the destination local or the source class head was borrowed, even though only a borrowed destination makes indirect uses non-dominated by the head definition. The PR removes the class-wide `borrowed_classes` bitset and rejects propagation only when `local` (the destination) is borrowed, allowing copies from a borrowed source head to a non-borrowed destination to be propagated. The updated MIR tests show the copy assignment disappearing and uses retargeted to the source local.
analysis.originalLogic: In `compute_copy_classes`, copy classes are built from direct copy/move assignments. The old code cloned `ssa.borrowed_locals()` into a `borrowed_classes` bitset keyed by class head, described as: "We must not unify two locals that are borrowed. But this is fine if one is borrowed and the other is not. This bitset is keyed by *class head* and contains whether any member of the class is borrowed." For each candidate `local = copy/move rhs`, it computed `let head = copies[rhs];` and rejected unification with "Do not unify borrowed locals." whenever `borrowed_classes.contains(local) || borrowed_classes.contains(head)`. When classes merged, it propagated borrowed status to the new head or `RETURN_PLACE`. Thus a borrowed member anywhere in either class blocked propagation.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historically, when the source/head local was borrowed but the destination local was not, CopyProp still declined to propagate. In `borrowed_local.borrowed`, the old output retained `_2 = copy _1;` and later used `_0 = opaque::<T>(copy _2)` instead of `_0 = opaque::<T>(copy _1)`. In `write_to_borrowed`, it retained `_4 = copy _5;` and used `dump_var::<char>(copy _4)` instead of `dump_var::<char>(copy _5)`. This was a missed optimization (conservative non-propagation), not a miscompile. The corrected transformation rejects unification only when `local` is borrowed: `if ssa.borrowed_locals().contains(local) { continue; }`.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies processed by CopyProp/SSA copy-class computation containing a direct local-to-local copy/move assignment `local = copy/move rhs`, where the source's equivalence-class head (`copies[rhs]`) is borrowed but the destination `local` is not borrowed. Examples include a generic value copied then the original borrowed (`fn borrowed<T: Copy + Freeze>(x: T)`), and a char copied, the source borrowed, and the destination later passed to `dump_var` (`write_to_borrowed`). Also includes larger inlined MIR such as `slice_filter.variant_a` where these propagations cascade.
analysis.trigger: A candidate `local = copy/move rhs` is seen where `head = copies[rhs]` belongs to a class containing a borrowed local, while `local` itself is not borrowed. CopyProp should then unify `local` with `head`, delete the copy assignment, and retarget uses of `local` to `head`. If `local` is borrowed, propagation must be rejected.
preconditions: The assignment is a direct `Rvalue::Use(Operand::Copy(place) | Operand::Move(place))` local-to-local copy/move.
The destination `local` is not borrowed; only a borrowed `local` triggers the rejection guard.
The definition of `head` dominates all uses of `local` (the source comment: "we need to ensure that the definition of `head` dominates all uses of `local`").
At most one of the two locals involved can be borrowed: `local` must not be borrowed, but `head` may be.
Removing the assignment is supported by direct-use accounting (`direct_uses[rhs] -= 1`).
pitfalls: Do not treat borrowing of the source/head as a blocker: the new guard checks only `ssa.borrowed_locals().contains(local)`.

Do not allow propagation when the destination `local` is borrowed; the source comment explains that then "there might exist an indirect use of `local` that isn't dominated by the definition, so we have to reject copy propagation."

Do not conflate post-copy overwrites/writes through borrows with the borrow restriction. The `write_to_borrowed` test still propagates from borrowed `_5` to non-borrowed `_4`; the legality condition is address observability plus domination, not the mere existence of an overwrite elsewhere.
The old `borrowed_classes` invariant and its propagation to `RETURN_PLACE` were removed; do not reintroduce class-wide borrowed tracking as the decision rule.
The `T: Copy + Freeze` bound in the regression test should not be mistaken for the pass's only condition; the implementation guard is about destination borrows.

When reading the outer MIR-opt `.diff` test updates, distinguish the removed old expectation lines from the new `+` expectation lines; the retained test name does not itself tell you which revision is corrected.
analysis.testStrategy: Add or update `tests/mir-opt/copy-prop/` tests using `mir!` plus `CHECK`/`CHECK-NEXT` assertions on exact local operands. Positive case: in `borrowed<T: Copy + Freeze>(x: T)`, after `let a = x; let b = &x;`, assert that `_2 = copy _1` is gone and the later call uses `_0 = opaque::<T>(copy _1)`. Positive case: in `write_to_borrowed`, after `_5 = _3; _6 = &_3; _4 = _5; ... _6 = &_5;`, assert that `_4 = copy _5` is gone and the call is `_7 = dump_var::<char>(copy _5)`. Add a negative control differing only by making the destination local borrowed (e.g. take `&a`/`&_2` and use it indirectly) and assert the copy assignment remains. Check both panic-abort and panic-unwind MIR diff variants, and verify broader pre-codegen expectations such as `slice_filter.variant_a-{closure#0}.PreCodegen.after.mir` reflect the extra propagation.
